Armed officers raced to the scene and engaged in a gunfight with the suspect, who was shot within three minutes of the attack beginning, preventing a further massacre, officials said. Krakow police said the suspected gunman died early on Monday morning. After the shooting, which began shortly before 15:00 local time (14:00 GMT) in Krakow's busy Main Market Square, police identified the attacker as a 24-year-old Polish man but did not confirm his name. In the hours after the shooting, a minister said early investigations indicate he was inspired by "far-right ideologies". The minister also described him as an "ultra-nationalist" without giving further details. Six people - four women and two men - are confirmed to have been killed in the attack. Four victims are Polish, while a British national and an Austrian woman were also killed. Poland's Prime Minister Donald Tusk said three bodies - two women and one man - were found at the gunman's house when it was searched after the attack. On Sunday, Polish police confirmed those three victims had been identified as the alleged gunman's 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother and 21-year-old sister. Polish media has reported the suspect had a firearms permit and may have obtained the weapons from his family home. Sixteen people, including five foreigners, two police officers and the attacker, were taken to hospital. The interior ministry later said they were from Austria, Britain, Germany, Portugal and Russia. The candidates selected to be astronauts would not only test spacecraft but would also live and work on the moon in a future moon base, said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman in a statement released on Saturday. "Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage," the statement said. "NASA's astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation." There are currently 32 active astronauts in NASA's astronaut corps. Since NASA missions began in the 1960s, the agency has selected 370 people to train as astronauts, according to the agency. The applicant process is extremely competitive. Out of more than 8,000 applicants for NASA's last astronaut class, only 10 candidates were selected. While any U.S. citizen can apply and there is no official age restriction, applicants will need to have a master's degree in a STEM-related field such as engineering or math. "Nursing degrees are now included in the STEM definition," Anna Schneider, NASA spokesperson, told NPR on Sunday. "Master's-level nursing degrees now meet the minimum educational requirement, whereas nursing degrees were previously excluded." In addition, NASA is requiring a minimum of three years of related professional experience after completing a degree. In lieu of a master's degree and working experience, NASA will consider those in a PhD program (in STEM), doctors or pilots with extensive flight experience. clusters.text: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman says CEO John Ternus is pressuring AI czar Craig Federighi to accelerate the Siri roadmap and deliver a powerful AI agent that can compete with OpenAI’s Dots or Meta’s Muse. While Federighi has delivered a functional version of Siri AI on an incredibly short timeline, the company has no illusions that it’s keeping pace with its rivals. Two significant improvements are expected to be made to Siri in the coming months. One will give the assistant fine-grained control over Apple’s first-party apps, allowing it to do things like rotate and crop images in Photos and organize Safari tabs. Those capabilities are expected to land with iOS 27.3. The bigger change, integration with third-party apps, is likely to land later, in the Spring, according to Gurman. That would let Siri place an order through Grubhub or book a dinner reservation through OpenTable, for example. But that’s just the start. Apple is expected to push Siri to become more agentic and enable features that will allow it to perform ongoing tasks, not just one-offs. Gurman says: > Dots, Muse and Grok can keep track of goals, determine what needs to happen next and continue pursuing objectives without the user initiating every individual step. Apple ultimately wants to go in this direction, I’m told, and I believe the company could make Siri more like an agent as early as next year — not that it has much of a choice, given current consumer and market demands.

clusters.text: Crystal Palace are poised to sack Pierre Sage after Sunday’s defeat by Liverpool left them bottom of the Premier League for the first time since December 2017, with Thomas Frank emerging as the main candidate to succeed him. The Frenchman, appointed in mid-June to replace Oliver Glasner, has been under mounting pressure since a 5-0 defeat by Brighton last month. There have been few signs of improvement as Palace have slumped to four successive league defeats. Sage has guided Palace to only two wins from their 10 Premier League games this season and they have the league’s worst defensive record, with 24 goals conceded so far. Although there were promising moments during the 3-1 defeat by Liverpool at Selhurst Park on Sunday, their habit of conceding goals from set pieces has not been rectified and it is understood the patience of the club’s hierarchy has worn thin despite Sage only being at the helm for 16 matches. He is expected to become the first Premier League manager to be sacked this season on Monday. Palace are already believed to have started the process of bringing in his replacement. Frank, who was dismissed by Tottenham in February, spoke to Palace in the summer and is said to be keen for a new challenge after a successful spell at Brentford. The former Nottingham Forest manager Sean Dyche also has his backers at Palace and would be seen as a safe pair of hands given his vast experience in the Premier League. Vítor Pereira, another former Forest manager, could be an alternative. Sage signed a three-year contract in south London after leaving Lens, where he won the Coupe de France and qualified for the Champions League in his final season. Palace have lost their two main central defenders this year, Marc Guéhi moving to Manchester City in January and Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea in the summer. Two loan players – Axel Disasi and the teenager Honest Ahanor – were signed as replacements. Palace did not land one of Sage’s top targets, Malick Fofana. clusters.text: Three leading consciousness researchers argue today's AI isn't conscious and probably can't be on silicon hardware. They reject the idea that running the right computations is enough for consciousness, challenging a central assumption in the debate. Anil Seth, Ned Block, and Giulio Tononi have spent decades researching consciousness from the perspectives of experimental neuroscience, theoretical neurobiology, and philosophy of mind. Their commentary responds to voices like biologist Richard Dawkins and AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton, who consider AI systems possibly already conscious. In their commentary for Nature, the authors also point to a study Anthropic published this year. The company reported internal processing patterns in Claude that resemble properties of consciously accessible information processing. Anthropic doesn't see this as evidence of subjective experience. The Butlin report agrees on today but leaves tomorrow open To understand the scope of the commentary, it helps to look at the report "Consciousness in Artificial Intelligence" by Patrick Butlin, Robert Long, and 17 other experts, including AI researcher Yoshua Bengio. The team drew on leading neuroscientific theories about how consciousness arises in the human brain and derived a kind of checklist with 14 indicators. The more of these an AI system meets, the stronger the case that it could be conscious. The researchers then evaluated several current systems, including large language models like GPT-4. The report concludes that none of the systems examined is a strong candidate for consciousness. On that point, it aligns with Seth, Block, and Tononi. For language models, Butlin and colleagues found only weak signs that the models meet the indicators of one of the most prominent consciousness theories at all. At the same time, the report sees no obvious technical barriers to building future AI systems that meet more indicators. Whether such systems would actually be conscious remains open. The authors specifically softened an earlier, stronger formulation on this point. There's also a foundational assumption. clusters.text: Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said no simulation could have predicted Max Verstappen's charge from 21st to second in the Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos. The Dutchman started near the back of the grid after an engine penalty and warned after qualifying that it would be harder to overtake at the São Paulo circuit than in previous years. But he proved himself wrong with an impressive drive to the podium. While speaking to the media after the race, Mekies was asked what Red Bull's simulations had said the Dutchman could do. "As always, I think no sim in the world will predict that you will go from P21 to P2 or that you get 14 places in five laps," the Frenchman explained. "There is no sim able to do that. So, he's beating the sim on a regular basis. Of course, it's frustrating [to start 21st] because the pace seemed good on Friday and also on Saturday morning, and in some respects in Q1 when we let him qualify. But it's part of the game, you know? "It's easy to forget it's the first year with the power unit. And the guys have been doing an extraordinary job, and we take the first penalty with Max this weekend, and that's what it is. It was not planned; we had a small issue on Friday that forced us to do so. But that's what it is." After parting ways with its power unit partner Honda at the end of 2025, Red Bull became a works team for 2026 with the introduction of Red Bull Powertrains, developed in collaboration with Ford. clusters.text: Chitrakoot (Uttar Pradesh) [India], November 9 (ANI): Four people died in an accident on the Jhansi-Mirzapur National Highway when a tractor-trolley carrying devotees returning from Chitrakoot, Uttar Pradesh, overturned, district officials said. According to Chitrakoot District Magistrate Pulkit Garg, the accident occurred due to the hook of the trolley coming out from the tractor near Ramnagar village on the National Highway under Raipura Police Station area. He said that five people were seriously injured and were referred to a hospital in Prayagraj, while seven sustained minor injuries. DM Pulkit Garg told reporters, "The vehicle involved was a truck— it was a tractor-trolley registered in MP. Most of the people were from Prayagraj and Rewa; they had come here for the Diwali fair and were on their way back to their respective homes. The hook connecting the tractor and the trolley failed—it came undone—causing the tractor and trolley to separate. The trolley veered off to the side of the road and overturned. As a result, four people died on the spot. Five people were seriously injured, and seven sustained minor injuries. The deceased were immediately taken to the nearest CHC in Ramnagar, where they received initial medical attention. Those who were seriously injured were promptly referred to Prayagraj via ambulance. The bodies of the deceased were sent to the district headquarters for post-mortem examinations." Further details are awaited. On Sunday, in a separate incident, a speeding car rammed into a scooter in Uttar Pradesh's Kanpur, resulting in the death of a man, police said. clusters.title: RBI steps up Financial Inclusion drive, Trains 8,700 Co-op Bank officials
clusters.text:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Nagpur, has stepped up efforts to strengthen financial inclusion and banking awareness in Vidarbha through three major initiatives, with a significant focus on building the capacity of cooperative banks and their personnel.

The initiatives include the nationwide Financial Inclusion Saturation Campaign, the PARAKH – Every Note Matters programme and the electronic Banking Awareness and Training (e-BAAT) programme.

Under the Financial Inclusion Saturation Campaign, being conducted by the Department of Financial Services (DFS), Ministry of Finance, in coordination with RBI and participating banks from October 21 to December 31, 2026, RBI's Financial Inclusion and Development Department (FIDD), Nagpur, is coordinating implementation across Vidarbha.

The campaign aims to organise at least one camp in every Gram Panchayat and Urban Local Body, bringing essential banking services closer to citizens.

The camps facilitate Re-KYC, C-KYC, nomination updates, Aadhaar seeding and activation of inoperative Jan-Dhan accounts. Citizens can also access enrolment facilities under PMJDY, PMJJBY, PMSBY and APY, along with assistance for Kisan Credit Card applications and information on crop insurance.

A major highlight is the PARAKH – Every Note Matters campaign, launched in January 2026, which directly benefits the cooperative banking sector. Over the past ten months, RBI Nagpur has trained more than 8,700 officials from 190 Urban Cooperative Banks (UCBs), 23 District Central Cooperative Banks (DCCBs), two State Cooperative Banks, two Regional Rural Banks and five commercial banks.

clusters.text: *Picture courtesy facebook.com shows Nisha Kumari Bhagat who had shared her picture on Facebook The death of tribal activist Nisha Kumari Bhagat in Ranchi, shortly after an emotional Facebook Live broadcast, has brought renewed attention to concerns over tribal rights, alleged land-related harassment and the protection available to those who raise their voices. Her allegations and the circumstances surrounding her death have prompted demands for an impartial investigation. Bhagat, around 38, originally from Gumla, was known for her work on tribal identity, culture, the Sarna faith and the protection of jal-jangal-zameen. She was also associated with the Jharkhand Loktantrik Krantikari Morcha and had contested the 2024 Assembly election from Gumla. In an approximately 11-minute Facebook Live session on November 6, she alleged harassment by land brokers and people connected with the administration. She spoke of seeking security and support, expressed disappointment over the lack of response to her grievances and appeared visibly distressed. She also raised concerns about online harassment and issues affecting tribal identity. Police found her dead at her Ranchi residence and registered an unnatural death case. No suicide note was recovered. Ranchi Rural SP Gaurav Goswami said all aspects, including her video, reported conversations and complaints, were being examined. Further action will depend on the investigation and post-mortem findings. Her father, Handu Bhagat, has demanded a CBI inquiry, alleging the involvement of influential people. The BJP has also sought a CBI probe, while CPI(ML) Liberation has called for a fair investigation. A symbolic protest was planned by members of the tribal community before her last rites at Uru village in Gumla. The tragedy calls for more than political exchanges. Allegations of intimidation and administrative inaction must be examined independently, with sensitivity and transparency. Protecting tribal rights also means ensuring that those who speak for their communities can seek help, be heard and access justice without fear. clusters.text: Real Madrid midfielder Bernardo Silva talked to the press after the team’s dominating 0-3 victory against Valencia in Mestalla, which allowed Los Blancos to put some pressure on Barcelona for their match against Atlético de Madrid. “A tough match, in a challenging atmosphere, against an aggressive team and a referee who allowed them to be aggressive. We want to keep winning and winning,” he added.
